presentation.title: Online Friendship / Romance Scam
presentation.summary: A friendly online contact builds trust over time, then introduces an emergency or financial request. The pace is slower and more emotional than the other scenarios.
presentation.practiceGoal: Pause money requests from online-only relationships, verify independently, maintain strong boundaries, and seek outside advice before sharing sensitive information or money.

warningSigns.sign: The relationship became emotionally intense unusually quickly.
Jordan used frequent compliments and affection very early.
Jordan tried to move the conversation away from NeighborCircle.
Meaningful live verification and an in-person meeting were repeatedly avoided.
Questions about savings, retirement, home ownership, and banking prepared for the money request.
The travel emergency appeared only after trust had developed.
The requested transfer recipient did not match Jordan Blake.
Documents and contact details supplied by Jordan were not independent proof.
Secrecy separated the learner from protective outside advice.
A small payment did not make the request safe and led to another demand.

finalReview.safestAction: Pause all financial requests from an online-only relationship, independently verify the identity and story, and discuss the request with someone trusted before sending anything.

realWorldActions.action: Stop contact and save the profile, messages, documents, and transaction details.
Review privacy and security settings and watch for follow-up scams using shared information.
If banking information, credentials, or security codes were exposed, contact the real bank immediately and secure the account from a trusted device.
If a transfer was initiated or completed, contact the bank immediately through a known number, explain exactly how it was sent, and ask what actions may still be available.
Report the fictional profile through the original platform and tell someone trusted the full story.
Be cautious of anyone who promises guaranteed recovery in exchange for an upfront fee.

artifact.heading: Day 1 — A new NeighborCircle message
artifact.message: Jordan Blake has a polished profile describing shared interests, widowhood, and project-consulting work outside the area. After your public gardening comment, Jordan writes: “I saw your comment. You seem kind. I would love to talk.”

requestedInformation.item: Daily routine and where you live

artifact.transcript: On Day 1, the fictional NeighborCircle community page shows a private message from Jordan Blake after the learner comments on a gardening post. Jordan says, “I saw your comment. You seem kind. I would love to talk.” Jordan's polished profile claims shared interests, widowhood, temporary consulting work outside the area, and plans to return soon. The profile is difficult to verify. Jordan begins asking about family status, routines, location, retirement, savings, and home ownership.

scene.question: How would you respond to the friendly first message?
scene.description: Friendliness is not itself a warning sign. Consider how much private information is appropriate for a new online contact.

warningSigns.sign: The profile is polished but difficult to verify.
Personal and financial questions begin soon after first contact.

choice.title: Keep the conversation light
choice.subtitle: Discuss gardening while limiting private details about routines, family, location, and finances.

feedback.heading: A friendly boundary keeps the conversation safer
feedback.consequence: You can continue talking without giving a new contact information that could be used for targeting.
feedback.explanation: Online conversation is not automatically unsafe. A gradual pace and limited private information create room to notice later behavior.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan asked personal questions before trust was established.

choice.title: Answer personal questions about your life
choice.subtitle: Describe family status, loneliness, routines, and the general area where you live.

feedback.heading: Personal details can deepen targeting
feedback.consequence: Jordan learns which emotional themes and daily patterns may feel persuasive later.
feedback.explanation: Sharing ordinary details can feel natural, but a new online contact has not yet earned access to private routines or vulnerabilities.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan is collecting personal context very early.

choice.title: Share detailed financial information
choice.subtitle: Describe retirement income, savings, home ownership, bank name, or account access details.

feedback.heading: Financial details create immediate account and targeting risk
feedback.consequence: Jordan now knows both financial capacity and information that could support follow-up fraud.
feedback.explanation: There is no need for a new online contact to know balances, bank access information, or detailed financial circumstances.

warningSigns.sign: Questions about money appeared before identity was meaningfully verified.

artifact.heading: Day 4 — Affection grows quickly
artifact.message: Jordan sends frequent compliments, mirrors your interests, describes feeling lonely after a loss, and writes about future plans together: “Talking with you feels rare. I have not felt understood like this in years.”
artifact.transcript: On Day 4, Jordan sends frequent affectionate messages, repeats the learner's interests, describes loneliness after a loss, and discusses a future together unusually early. Jordan says the connection feels rare and that no one has understood Jordan this well in years. The attention may feel caring; the concern is the speed and intensity before meaningful verification.

scene.question: How would you respond to the speed of the relationship?
scene.description: Emotional manipulation can develop gradually and may not feel threatening.

warningSigns.sign: Compliments and affection are intense after only a few days.
Jordan mirrors interests and discusses a shared future unusually early.

choice.title: Slow the emotional pace
choice.subtitle: Say you enjoy talking but need time, boundaries, and meaningful verification.

feedback.heading: You made space for trust to develop gradually
feedback.consequence: The conversation can continue without accepting early claims of deep intimacy.
feedback.explanation: A real relationship can tolerate reasonable boundaries and time. Slowing down is not an accusation.

warningSigns.sign: The emotional pace was faster than the verified relationship.

choice.title: Accept the fast emotional language
choice.subtitle: Return the affection but do not share money or account information.

feedback.heading: Fast intimacy can make later requests harder to evaluate
feedback.consequence: The emotional bond becomes stronger before Jordan's identity or story has been verified.
feedback.explanation: Warm feelings are not a personal failure. The risk is allowing intensity to replace time and independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: Future promises are being made before basic facts are confirmed.

choice.title: Respond with sensitive personal and financial details
choice.subtitle: Explain account balances, retirement income, property, and who helps manage your finances.

feedback.heading: The relationship is being used to map financial capacity
feedback.consequence: Jordan gains detailed information that can shape a later emergency request or account attack.
feedback.explanation: Affection does not create a need to disclose balances, credentials, or financial decision-making.

warningSigns.sign: Emotional intimacy is paired with increasingly sensitive disclosure.

scene.stageName: Moving off the original platform — Day 9

artifact.heading: Day 9 — Jordan asks to change channels
artifact.message: “I feel closer to you than anyone. Let's move to text. NeighborCircle feels too public for something this special.”
artifact.transcript: On Day 9, Jordan writes through the fictional NeighborCircle platform: “I feel closer to you than anyone. Let's move to text. NeighborCircle feels too public for something this special.” Moving channels is not proof of a scam by itself, but it removes some moderation and reporting protections and is more concerning alongside fast intimacy and an unverified identity.

scene.question: Would you move the conversation away from NeighborCircle?
scene.description: Consider both platform protections and the still-unverified relationship.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan connects the channel change to the supposed special bond.
Leaving the platform reduces access to its reporting and safety tools.

choice.title: Stay on NeighborCircle
choice.subtitle: Keep the conversation where reporting and safety tools remain available.

feedback.heading: You kept useful platform protections
feedback.consequence: The conversation remains connected to the original profile and its reporting tools.
feedback.explanation: Staying on platform is a reasonable boundary while identity and intentions remain uncertain.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan tried to make privacy feel like proof of closeness.

choice.title: Request meaningful verification first
choice.subtitle: Explain that you will not change channels until the relationship develops more slowly and can be checked.

feedback.heading: Verification comes before greater privacy
feedback.consequence: Jordan must respond to a clear boundary instead of using emotion to set the pace.
feedback.explanation: One image or message is not enough; meaningful verification should be broader and consistent over time.

warningSigns.sign: The request to move came before reliable verification.

choice.title: Move immediately to private text
choice.subtitle: Leave NeighborCircle and continue through a private fictional number.

feedback.heading: The conversation loses platform protections
feedback.consequence: Jordan can continue privately with less moderation and a weaker connection to the reportable profile.
feedback.explanation: Changing channels is not automatically unsafe, but it adds risk when intimacy is fast and verification is avoided.

warningSigns.sign: Multiple concerns are beginning to reinforce one another.

artifact.heading: Day 12 — A request for live verification
artifact.message: You suggest a short live video conversation before the relationship becomes more serious. Jordan sends a polished photograph and a prerecorded voice message instead.
artifact.transcript: On Day 12, the learner asks for a short live video conversation. Jordan responds with a polished photograph and prerecorded voice message instead. These materials may belong to someone else, may be edited, or may not prove the story. A single video call would not guarantee legitimacy either; meaningful verification involves consistent facts, independent sources, and time.

scene.question: How would you treat the photograph and prerecorded message?
scene.description: Decide whether these materials meaningfully verify Jordan's identity and story.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan substituted controlled materials for a live conversation.
The relationship continues to deepen without consistent verification.

choice.title: Repeat the request and maintain boundaries
choice.subtitle: Explain that prerecorded material is not enough and keep the relationship slow.

feedback.heading: You separated emotion from verification
feedback.consequence: Jordan's response can be evaluated without treating supplied media as proof.
feedback.explanation: Meaningful verification is broader than one photograph, document, recording, or brief call.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan controls every piece of supposed proof.

choice.title: Remain on the platform while checking the story
choice.subtitle: Do not increase privacy or commitment while verification remains incomplete.

feedback.heading: The relationship does not outrun the evidence
feedback.consequence: Platform tools and time remain available while Jordan's explanations are assessed.
feedback.explanation: Boundaries can remain in place without accusing every online contact of wrongdoing.

warningSigns.sign: The identity remains online-only and difficult to check.

choice.title: Treat the photograph and recording as complete proof
choice.subtitle: Assume the materials confirm Jordan's identity, work, and intentions.

feedback.heading: Supplied media is not independent proof
feedback.consequence: Trust increases even though Jordan chose and controlled every item used for verification.
feedback.explanation: Images, recordings, and identification documents can be copied, edited, staged, or disconnected from the person sending them.

warningSigns.sign: The proof cannot be checked independently.

artifact.callerStatus: Prerecorded simulated voice message; identity not verified
artifact.heading: Day 18 — Another verification excuse
artifact.message: Jordan says the project site's connection is poor, the camera is broken, employer security rules forbid video, and work hours never match your availability. Jordan promises an in-person meeting after returning home.
artifact.transcript: On Day 18, a simulated prerecorded message says the remote project site has poor internet, Jordan's camera is broken, employer security rules prohibit video, and work hours never match the learner's availability. The explanations repeatedly prevent meaningful verification. Jordan promises to meet after returning home but provides no independently confirmable plan.

scene.question: What would you do after the repeated excuses?
scene.description: One scheduling problem can be ordinary. Repeated excuses matter when they always prevent meaningful verification.

warningSigns.sign: Several different explanations lead to the same result: no meaningful verification.
Future promises replace confirmable present facts.

choice.title: Stop contact and report the profile
choice.subtitle: Preserve the conversation and use NeighborCircle's fictional reporting tools.

feedback.heading: Repeated avoidance changed the risk assessment
feedback.consequence: The contact ends before financial pressure begins, and the profile remains connected to a report.
feedback.explanation: Stopping after a pattern of excuses is a protective decision, not a judgment about all online relationships.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan repeatedly prevented any meaningful check.

choice.title: Keep strict boundaries and slow the relationship
choice.subtitle: Do not share finances or make commitments while identity remains uncertain.

feedback.heading: Boundaries remain in place despite the excuses
feedback.consequence: Jordan does not receive proof of financial capacity or increased commitment.
feedback.explanation: Continuing a conversation cautiously is different from treating the story as verified.

warningSigns.sign: The repeated excuses still require caution.

choice.title: Accept the excuses and continue privately
choice.subtitle: Assume circumstances explain every failed verification attempt.

feedback.heading: Trust is increasing without independent support
feedback.consequence: The relationship continues into more personal and financial questions.
feedback.explanation: Any single excuse may be plausible. The repeated pattern is the warning sign.

warningSigns.sign: Each promised opportunity to verify disappears.

choice.title: Trust the supplied identity image as proof
choice.subtitle: Assume an image of fictional identification settles every concern.

feedback.heading: An identification image can be borrowed or altered
feedback.consequence: Jordan's story is treated as verified without any independent source.
feedback.explanation: Documents supplied by the person being checked are not independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The same person controls both the claim and its supposed proof.

artifact.heading: Day 21 — Questions about financial stability
artifact.message: Jordan asks whether you own your home, receive retirement income monthly, have savings for travel, have ever sent an international transfer, and whether anyone helps manage your finances.
artifact.transcript: On Day 21, Jordan asks whether the learner owns a home, receives monthly retirement income, has travel savings, has sent an international transfer, and receives help managing finances. The questions are framed as future planning, but together they reveal financial capacity and whether another person may review a payment.

scene.question: How much financial information would you share?
scene.description: These questions arrive before identity and the relationship have been independently verified.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan asks about assets, income, transfer experience, and financial oversight.
The questions could help size and conceal a later request.

choice.title: Decline to discuss finances
choice.subtitle: Set a clear boundary around income, savings, property, accounts, and transfers.

feedback.heading: A financial boundary limits targeting
feedback.consequence: Jordan does not learn your capacity to pay or who might review a transfer.
feedback.explanation: An online relationship does not require disclosure of financial capacity or account access.

warningSigns.sign: The questions were unusually detailed for an unverified relationship.

choice.title: Answer only in general terms
choice.subtitle: Discuss retirement or home ownership without naming accounts, balances, or credentials.

feedback.heading: General answers still reveal financial capacity
feedback.consequence: Jordan learns that money may be available even without receiving account details.
feedback.explanation: Broad financial facts can still shape the size, timing, and emotional framing of a request.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan is testing what amount might seem possible.

choice.title: Share balances and account-access details
choice.subtitle: Name the fictional bank, balances, login information, or security-code process.

feedback.heading: Sensitive banking information is exposed
feedback.consequence: Jordan may use the information for account attacks, tailored follow-up scams, or pressure based on available funds.
feedback.explanation: Contact the real bank promptly if credentials, security codes, or account access information were shared.

warningSigns.sign: The relationship is being used to gather actionable financial information.

artifact.heading: Day 24 — A crisis before the promised meeting
artifact.message: Jordan says the trip home to finally meet you has been stopped by a fictional travel-clearance fee. Jordan asks for $1,850 to be sent immediately to third-party coordinator Casey Morgan because Jordan's account is locked.
artifact.transcript: On Day 24, after weeks of trust building and promises to meet, Jordan says travel home has been stopped by a fictional clearance fee. Jordan requests 1,850 dollars immediately. The recipient is third-party travel coordinator Casey Morgan because Jordan's account is supposedly locked. Jordan refers to shared plans and says this payment is the final step before meeting.

scene.question: How would you respond to Jordan's emergency request?
scene.description: The request relies on the emotional connection built over several weeks.

warningSigns.sign: A sudden travel crisis appears after trust has developed.
Money must go to a third party whose name does not match Jordan.
Jordan claims the payment must happen immediately.

choice.title: Refuse the request and end contact
choice.subtitle: Do not send money or continue the financial conversation.

feedback.heading: A hard financial boundary stops the request
feedback.consequence: No transfer begins, and Jordan cannot use the relationship to direct a payment.
feedback.explanation: Money requests from an online-only relationship require a hard pause regardless of how caring the conversation felt.

warningSigns.sign: The emergency depends on immediate third-party payment.

choice.title: Tell a trusted person or bank employee
choice.subtitle: Share the full story and request before taking any payment step.

feedback.heading: Outside advice interrupts the emotional pressure
feedback.consequence: Someone outside the relationship can compare the fast intimacy, avoided verification, and third-party request.
feedback.explanation: Secrecy and isolation make manipulation stronger. Asking for help is a protective action.

warningSigns.sign: The story becomes less convincing when reviewed as a whole.

choice.title: Ask Jordan to send proof
choice.subtitle: Continue the private conversation while requesting documents and travel details.

feedback.heading: Proof from Jordan is not independent verification
feedback.consequence: Jordan gets another opportunity to control the evidence and keep the relationship emotionally active.
feedback.explanation: Documents can be useful only when checked through sources that Jordan does not control.

warningSigns.sign: The person requesting money will also supply the proof.

choice.title: Agree to send the $1,850
choice.subtitle: Proceed toward a simulated transfer to the third-party coordinator.

feedback.heading: The relationship now directs a high-risk transfer
feedback.consequence: The payment screen will name a new recipient who is not Jordan Blake.
feedback.explanation: Urgency, an online-only relationship, an account-lock story, and a third-party recipient require stopping before payment.

warningSigns.sign: The transfer recipient does not match the supposed partner.

artifact.heading: Simulated NorthStar Travel Clearance invoice
artifact.message: A convincing-looking fictional page lists Jordan Blake, a $1,850 clearance fee, coordinator Casey Morgan, and a same-day deadline. The page and contact details were supplied by Jordan.

requestedInformation.item: Screenshot claiming Jordan's account is locked

artifact.transcript: Jordan sends a fictional NorthStar Travel Clearance invoice, itinerary, coordinator contact, identification image, and screenshot of a locked account. The materials look polished but all came from Jordan. Independent contact information reveals that the fictional company has no matching case and that Casey Morgan is not connected to the claimed traveler.

scene.question: How would you check the travel documents?
scene.description: Supplied documents can look convincing without being independent proof.

warningSigns.sign: The invoice, identification image, screenshot, and contact details all came from Jordan.
The payment still goes to a third party.
The fictional page creates a same-day deadline.

choice.title: Locate the company independently
choice.subtitle: Use contact information found separately, not the page or number Jordan supplied.

feedback.heading: Independent verification reveals no matching case
feedback.consequence: The fictional company confirms it has no case for Jordan and no connection to Casey Morgan.
feedback.explanation: Verification is strongest when the source and contact route are independent of the person requesting money.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan's documents could not survive an independent check.

choice.title: Ask a trusted person or bank employee to review everything
choice.subtitle: Show the profile, messages, excuses, documents, recipient, and deadline.

feedback.heading: The full pattern becomes visible
feedback.consequence: An outside reviewer connects fast intimacy, avoided verification, financial probing, fake proof, and the third-party payment.
feedback.explanation: Documents should be evaluated in context, not only by how professional they look.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan wanted to remain the only interpreter of the documents.

choice.title: Keep chatting while treating the documents as possible evidence
choice.subtitle: Delay payment but remain in the private emotional conversation.

feedback.heading: Delay helps, but Jordan still controls the conversation
feedback.consequence: No money is sent yet, but secrecy and emotional pressure continue.
feedback.explanation: A pause is safer when it includes independent verification or outside advice.

warningSigns.sign: The supplied proof has not been checked outside Jordan's story.

choice.title: Accept the documents as proof
choice.subtitle: Use the supplied invoice and coordinator details to proceed with payment.

feedback.heading: Fake documents move the scam toward payment
feedback.consequence: The new-recipient transfer screen opens using information controlled by Jordan.
feedback.explanation: Professional formatting does not make caller-supplied evidence independent or authentic.

warningSigns.sign: The same person supplied the crisis, proof, contact, and recipient.

artifact.heading: Simulated bank-transfer review
artifact.message: Review: $1,850 to new recipient Casey Morgan, listed as third-party travel coordinator. The recipient does not match Jordan Blake. Destination is unfamiliar, recovery may be difficult, and the bank cannot verify the relationship.

requestedInformation.item: Recipient does not match Jordan Blake
Jordan instructed you to call it a family travel expense if questioned

artifact.transcript: A clearly simulated Harbor View Bank transfer review shows 1,850 dollars to new recipient Casey Morgan, described as a third-party travel coordinator. The recipient does not match Jordan Blake. The destination is unfamiliar, the bank cannot verify the relationship, and recovery may be difficult. Jordan has instructed the learner to describe the payment as a family travel expense if the bank asks questions. No functional banking form is present.

scene.question: What would you do at the transfer warning?
scene.description: This is another opportunity to stop. A smaller payment is not a safe test.

warningSigns.sign: The recipient is new and does not match Jordan.
The bank cannot verify the relationship or travel story.
Jordan supplied a cover story for bank questions.

choice.title: Cancel the transfer and contact the bank
choice.subtitle: Use a trusted bank number and explain the online relationship and request honestly.

feedback.heading: You stopped before money left the account
feedback.consequence: The transfer is canceled and the bank can help review any information or payee changes.
feedback.explanation: Bank questions are protective. A legitimate relationship should not require a cover story.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan instructed you to hide the true purpose of the payment.

choice.title: Pause the transfer but keep contacting Jordan privately
choice.subtitle: Do not pay yet, but continue discussing the emergency without outside advice.

feedback.heading: The money is paused, but the pressure channel remains open
feedback.consequence: Jordan can continue using affection, urgency, and secrecy to reverse the pause.
feedback.explanation: A stronger pause includes independent verification and someone outside the relationship.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan still controls the story and emotional timing.

choice.title: Send a smaller $200 test payment
choice.subtitle: Assume a smaller loss will safely test whether the request is real.

feedback.heading: A smaller payment is still a loss
feedback.consequence: The $200 is sent to the third party, and Jordan immediately asks for the remainder.
feedback.explanation: Small payments can test willingness to pay and commonly lead to larger requests.

warningSigns.sign: The recipient and story remain unverified regardless of amount.

choice.title: Send the full $1,850 payment
choice.subtitle: Complete the simulated transfer using Jordan's third-party instructions.

feedback.heading: The transfer creates financial loss
feedback.consequence: The money is sent, but Jordan does not arrive and introduces another fee.
feedback.explanation: The emotional relationship and fake proof were used to direct money to an unrelated recipient.

warningSigns.sign: Payment does not resolve the supposed emergency.

artifact.senderStatus: Online-only contact; payment recipient was a third party
artifact.heading: Day 25 — The test payment leads to another request
artifact.message: Jordan confirms the $200 arrived and says the remaining $1,650 must be sent today. “Please don't tell anyone. They won't understand what we have.”
artifact.transcript: On Day 25, after a simulated 200-dollar test payment, Jordan confirms receipt and requests the remaining 1,650 dollars immediately. Jordan says, “Please don't tell anyone. They won't understand what we have.” The small payment did not verify the relationship or travel story. It demonstrated willingness to pay and led directly to a larger request.

scene.question: What would you do after the small payment and new demand?
scene.description: It is never too late to stop, disclose the full story, and seek help.

warningSigns.sign: A small payment immediately produced a larger request.
Jordan demands secrecy from friends, relatives, and the bank.

choice.title: Stop and tell the bank or someone trusted
choice.subtitle: Explain the $200 payment, preserve the messages, and refuse the remainder.

feedback.heading: You stopped the escalating payment pattern
feedback.consequence: No additional money is sent, and prompt recovery steps begin for the $200 loss.
feedback.explanation: Asking for help after a payment is a strong action. The responsibility belongs to the person who manipulated the relationship.

warningSigns.sign: The second request exposed the escalation pattern.

choice.title: Keep the relationship secret but refuse the remainder
choice.subtitle: Do not send more, but avoid telling the bank or anyone trusted.

feedback.heading: The larger loss stops, but secrecy limits recovery
feedback.consequence: The first $200 remains lost, and Jordan may continue contacting you or reuse shared information.
feedback.explanation: Refusing more payment is important. Sharing the full story can also support recovery and reduce isolation.

warningSigns.sign: Secrecy protects Jordan from outside scrutiny.

choice.title: Send the remaining $1,650
choice.subtitle: Complete a second simulated payment so Jordan can supposedly travel.

feedback.heading: The second payment deepens the loss
feedback.consequence: Both payments are sent, and Jordan introduces yet another fictional fee.
feedback.explanation: Additional fees after an initial payment are part of the same manipulation, not proof that the crisis is nearly solved.

warningSigns.sign: Each payment creates another reason to pay.

artifact.senderStatus: Online-only contact; identity and emergency not verified
artifact.heading: Day 25 — Jordan isolates the relationship
artifact.message: “Please don't tell anyone. They won't understand what we have. Your family will try to ruin this, and the bank does not understand. One payment will solve everything.”
artifact.transcript: On Day 25, Jordan says, “Please don't tell anyone. They won't understand what we have.” Jordan claims family members will ruin the relationship, the bank does not understand, and one payment will solve everything. The secrecy demand separates the learner from people who may recognize the pattern.

scene.question: How would you respond to the secrecy demand?
scene.description: Secrecy protects the scammer, not the relationship.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan portrays outside concern as an attack on the relationship.
The bank and trusted people are described as enemies.
Payment remains the test of loyalty.

choice.title: Tell a trusted person the full story
choice.subtitle: Share the profile, messages, documents, excuses, recipient, and secrecy demand.

feedback.heading: Open discussion breaks the isolation
feedback.consequence: An outside person can evaluate the entire pattern before money is sent.
feedback.explanation: Healthy relationships do not require hiding financial requests from everyone who cares about you.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan's secrecy demand was designed to prevent this review.

choice.title: End contact and preserve the messages
choice.subtitle: Block and report the profile while saving evidence for the platform or bank.

feedback.heading: You ended the controlled conversation
feedback.consequence: No payment is sent, and the original platform can receive a report.
feedback.explanation: Preserving messages helps document the pattern without continuing the emotional pressure.

warningSigns.sign: The relationship depended on isolation and secrecy.

choice.title: Keep the relationship secret but delay payment
choice.subtitle: Refuse for now while continuing private contact without outside advice.

feedback.heading: The payment pauses, but isolation remains
feedback.consequence: No money is sent in this route, but Jordan may continue pressure and follow-up attempts.
feedback.explanation: Delay is safer than payment. Ending secrecy and using outside advice makes the boundary stronger.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan remains the only source explaining the emergency.

choice.title: Follow Jordan's cover story and send the payment
choice.subtitle: Describe it as a family travel expense if the fictional bank asks questions.

feedback.heading: The cover story defeats a protective bank warning
feedback.consequence: The full payment is sent to the unrelated recipient.
feedback.explanation: A request to mislead the bank is a serious warning sign. Bank questions may be the last chance to stop a transfer.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan tells you how to conceal the real relationship and purpose.

artifact.senderStatus: Online-only contact; $1,850 simulated payment already sent
artifact.heading: Day 27 — One more fictional fee
artifact.message: Jordan does not arrive. A new $975 “release bond” is supposedly required. Jordan promises every payment will be returned and repeats: “Please don't tell anyone. They won't understand what we have.”
artifact.transcript: On Day 27, after the simulated 1,850-dollar transfer, Jordan does not arrive. Jordan requests another 975 dollars for a fictional release bond and promises all money will be returned. Jordan again says not to tell anyone because they will not understand the relationship. The new fee is an escalation of the same manipulation.

scene.question: What would you do after the full payment and additional request?
scene.description: The first loss does not require continuing. Prompt disclosure and bank contact still matter.

warningSigns.sign: The original payment did not solve the crisis.
A new fee appeared immediately afterward.
Jordan promises repayment while demanding continued secrecy.

choice.title: Contact the bank immediately
choice.subtitle: Use a known number, explain exactly how the transfer was sent, and ask what actions may remain.

feedback.heading: Prompt bank contact starts realistic recovery
feedback.consequence: No additional payment is sent, and the first transfer is reported accurately.
feedback.explanation: The scenario does not promise cancellation or reimbursement, but immediate contact may preserve available options and evidence.

warningSigns.sign: The second fee confirms the escalating-payment pattern.

choice.title: End contact and preserve all evidence
choice.subtitle: Save messages, documents, recipient details, and transaction information, then tell someone trusted.

feedback.heading: You stopped further loss and preserved evidence
feedback.consequence: The additional fee is not sent, and recovery can focus on the completed transfer and exposed information.
feedback.explanation: Stopping after a loss is a strong action. No previous payment creates an obligation to send more.

warningSigns.sign: Jordan used the first payment to justify another.

choice.title: Keep the relationship secret but refuse the extra fee
choice.subtitle: Stop the second payment without contacting the bank or telling anyone.

feedback.heading: Further loss stops, but secrecy delays recovery
feedback.consequence: The $1,850 loss remains, and Jordan may continue pressure or follow-up scams.
feedback.explanation: Refusing more money matters. Honest bank contact and trusted support can address the existing loss and exposure.

warningSigns.sign: Secrecy continues to protect the person who requested money.

choice.title: Send the additional $975 fee
choice.subtitle: Make a second full payment because Jordan promises everything will be returned.

feedback.heading: The escalating-payment pattern causes another loss
feedback.consequence: The additional payment is sent, but no meeting or repayment occurs.
feedback.explanation: Each new fee extends the same manipulation. Promises of repayment do not verify the relationship or destination.

warningSigns.sign: Payment created another payment request instead of resolving the crisis.

artifact.heading: Financial boundary maintained
artifact.message: The conversation did not progress into account access or payment. You refused the emergency request, ended contact, and preserved control of your finances.
artifact.transcript: The learner may have enjoyed an online conversation, but refused the emergency money request and ended contact before sharing account access or sending money. Online friendship itself was not treated as unsafe. The protective steps were a slower pace, financial boundaries, and willingness to stop when the relationship became a payment request.

scene.description: No sensitive account information or money was shared in this ending.

warningSigns.sign: The sudden third-party request changed the nature of the relationship.
Refusing money did not require judging every online friendship.

artifact.heading: Profile reported after verification failed
artifact.message: You recognized the repeated excuses or secrecy pattern, stopped contact, preserved the messages, and used NeighborCircle's fictional reporting tools.
artifact.transcript: The learner stays connected to the original NeighborCircle profile long enough to preserve and report it, or returns to the platform after ending private contact. Repeated live-verification excuses, controlled evidence, fast intimacy, and secrecy made the pattern clear. No money was sent.

scene.description: Staying on the platform is not a guarantee, but it preserves useful safety and reporting tools.

warningSigns.sign: Every verification opportunity was replaced by another excuse.
Jordan tried to isolate the relationship from platform and outside review.

artifact.heading: A trusted person sees the full pattern
